card.band: 8 h. The explainer is easy. Checkpoint re-evaluation and exact semantic parity with the real scheduler across wildcards, ruleorder and params-triggered reruns separate runs. A frontier agent reaches about half. A weaker model delivers only the simple reasons.
card.cheat: Printing the plan from the existing --dry-run text: the JSON contract and critical path need dag internals. Hidden Snakefiles and states are not visible.
card.grading: Hidden behavioural tests over several hundred generated Snakefiles and working-tree states: exact JSON plan, ordering and critical-path values. The repo's existing suite is a regression gate. Credit per feature bucket.
card.reference: Our reference, written by us, is about 1500-2000 added lines across the dag, persistence and CLI modules.
card.task: /app ships a snapshot of snakemake at the pinned commit. The agent adds a multi-part feature set: a --plan-json explainer that emits per-job reasons (missing output, changed code/params/input, forced), a --what-if option that simulates a changed file, and a per-rule cost estimator with critical-path calculation. It also adds checkpoint-aware re-evaluation planning without executing jobs. Everything is reached through the CLI and the Python API.
card.title: Snakemake checkpointed DAG introspection and what-if planner

facts.claim: Snakemake already prints a per-job reason in dry-run (--reason / printreason, shown as a reason: line per job)
The current stable CLI page lists a flag that prints job reasons directly
No plan-JSON, what-if or cost-estimation flag is documented in the stable CLI

Open PRs (page 1 of 9 checked) contain no JSON job-plan output, job-reason, cost-estimation or changed-file simulation work; closest are #4318 (dry-run protected output checks), #4338, #4279 (elapsed time logging)
Release notes for v9.27.0 do not mention job reasons, checkpoints or DAG/job plan output

full_card.band: Seed claims 8 h tier with about half reached by frontier; no dated public evidence. Own estimate: excellent frontier agent needs about 10 h for whole scope, so 20 h tier fits better. Partial buckets: explainer (reasons), what-if, cost/critical path, checkpoint replanning, then exact parity across wildcards, ruleorder, params reruns.
full_card.build_cost: smoke_build empty (not run); pure Python so build is likely easy, but the suite is 2029 test files and needs a subset plan. Our reference plus hidden generator and per-bucket graders est. 3-4 days (below K12 5-day limit).
full_card.deliverable: CLI and Python API: --plan-json explainer with per-job reasons (missing output, changed code/params/input, forced); --what-if simulating a changed file; per-rule cost estimator with critical-path values; checkpoint-aware re-evaluation planning without running jobs.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden Snakefiles and states never shipped. Printing plan from existing --dry-run text fails the JSON contract and critical-path checks. Edits to tests or build config are caught by hidden re-run from clean snapshot; regression gate runs the untouched suite.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden behavioural tests over several hundred generated Snakefiles and working-tree states: exact JSON plan, ordering, critical-path values; credit per feature bucket; repo suite as regression gate.
full_card.local_fit: Pure Python, CPU only, no network needed at run time; fits 8 cores / 16 GB.
full_card.lookup: partial: --reason (printreason) already emits per-job reasons; no plan-JSON, what-if or cost flag documented; no open PR implementing them on page 1 of 9.
full_card.provenance: snakemake/snakemake @ v9.27.0 (head 1c67a66), MIT, released 2026-09-11, Python, 2888 stars (GitHub API).
full_card.reference: Team-written reference, about 1500-2000 added lines across dag, persistence and CLI modules; not public. Live parity oracle available in-image via the real scheduler's existing reasons.
full_card.ships: History-less snapshot of the pinned commit in /app; reference, hidden generator and hidden states excluded.
full_card.similarity: Public task neighbours max 0.089 (what-will-my-model-forget, shortest_path_dijkstra), under 0.15. Seed neighbour S-im-073 at 0.255 and S-im-088 at 0.208 need a content check for overlap, not a kill.

spike_plan.kill_if: Build or the targeted suite cannot run in the container, or reason output varies between runs so exact-JSON parity cannot be graded.
spike_plan.pass_if: Build succeeds offline after install, reason output is deterministic across two runs, the targeted suite subset runs cleanly, and the checkpoint case re-evaluates in dry-run.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, clone snakemake at 1c67a66 and install editable with its test dependencies (the smoke_build was empty, so this is the first real build check).
Write three tiny Snakefiles: one with wildcards, one with ruleorder, one with a params change and an input change; run the real scheduler with -n and the reason flag to capture reference reasons.
Run a targeted subset of the existing suite on the scheduler paths those Snakefiles touch and record pass/fail counts and runtime.
Add a checkpoint Snakefile and confirm the real scheduler re-evaluates it in dry-run without executing jobs; capture the output.
Run the same Snakefiles twice to check that reason output is deterministic.
Count how many distinct reason categories and checkpoint paths the three Snakefiles exercise to check the bucket split.

v1.summary: Snakemake v9.27.0 (MIT, released 2026-09-11) is real, and the card's claims about the repo check out, though --reason already prints per-job reasons, so the explainer is partly lookup-able and a parity oracle exists in-image. No gate fails, so the seed passes to spike with a 20 h tier, since the card's 8 h budget looks short for a roughly 10 h frontier scope.

v2.note: Real repo, but the features are invented: no issue or PR asks for them. The JSON contract, the cost model and the critical-path semantics are ours, so exact-JSON grading against our unwritten reference risks rejecting reasonable designs. A maintainer is unlikely to accept 'checkpoint re-evaluation without executing' as specified, because checkpoint outputs are unknown before the job runs. --reason already exists, which makes the explainer bucket easy. Keep only if the spec is pinned in detail and grading checks semantic fields rather than the exact layout.
